text: Customer reports are evidence, weighed lightly. Customers report outages through the Meralco App, SMS, the hotline, Facebook and X, and each report is linked to the equipment job it is about. Reports are evidence, not orders. They never override the safety check, flood clearance, the customer tier or the number of customers a job restores. Their number is used only where the hierarchy already places it: among eligible jobs with the same tier and the same customers restored, the job with more linked reports goes first. One report does not move a job up, however alarming it sounds. Reactions, shares, and repeated posts by the same person are not more reports.

metadata.title: Customer reports are evidence, weighed lightly

text: What customer reports say is read for the crew, not for the ranking. Read the linked reports for two things. First, hazards: when a report describes a live wire, sparks, a fallen or leaning pole, or a tree on the line at a job that is marked Safe, note it for the crew to confirm on arrival. When three or more separate people describe the same hazard at a job marked Safe, say that its safety status should be re-checked before the truck is sent. Second, people who depend on power: note any mention of oxygen, dialysis, a nebulizer, or a bedridden or elderly person, so the crew and customer care know. Neither of these changes the order by itself. Reports describing a hazard at a job already marked Unsafe simply agree with that status.
